biography.plain_text: John Young Sangster, known as Jack, was a British industrialist who made his fortune by rebuilding motorcycle businesses. He worked in his father's engineering company before buying its assets from receivers and establishing Ariel Motors. He also acquired Triumph, sold both manufacturers to BSA and eventually became chairman of the group.
biography.html: John Young Sangster, known as Jack, was a British industrialist who made his fortune by rebuilding motorcycle businesses. He worked in his father's engineering company before buying its assets from receivers and establishing Ariel Motors. He also acquired Triumph, sold both manufacturers to BSA and eventually became chairman of the group.

confidence.reason: Specialist biography, contemporary reporting and archival business history support the full-name identity, family industrial platform and acquisition career.

long_biography.plain_text:
Motorcycle industrialist Jack Sangster also designed a small, inexpensive car. Rover bought the design and recruited him to oversee production of the model that became the Rover Eight. His technical background preceded a business career in which he placed considerable authority in the hands of specialist designers and managers.

As BSA chairman, he brought younger non-executive directors onto the board and gave shareholders fuller accounts of the group's performance. He also supported Edward Turner's determination to keep Triumph's Meriden operation largely autonomous within the larger organisation, preserving the marque's separate identity and management.
